main_text.p: ne homines isti mores suos, & dogmata vlla ex parte patientur immutari, qui tantum nobis su-percilium offenderunt. Et ne longe a materia difcedamus, Stephanus Papa Epistola ad eundem Basilium, cum ille postremo suæ vitæ tempore seductus a Photio contra Papam Marinum crimina intendens scripsisset, rerum temporalium curam & principatum Imperatoribus, spiritualium summis Pontificibus traditam esse palam prædicat; & Ioannes solo nutu Imperatoris Photium restitutum, & tantam Romanæ Ecclesiæ iniuriam illatam tolerasset? Pulso rursum Photio a Leone Imperatore Stylianus Neocæsareæ Episcopus petit sui aliorumque Episcoporum, & Clericorum, quod communicauerint cum Photio restitutionem, & Stephanus respondet; Ἡμᾶς αὔ δ᾽ ἀκειβῶς ἐξετάσεως [?] οἰκονομίας [?] ἐπιγνῶναι κείσεται [?]. Διὸ καὶ αὐτὸς τῶν Φώτιον [?] παρεδρά[?]μομεν, καὶ χρεία ἐστὶν ἐνὸς ἐκ τοῦ μέσου [?] ἐπισκόπους [?] ὑποσαλεύων, ὡς αὐτὸς ἐξεταζουλῶν [?] πάσης ἀμφιβολίας, ἐκ πάντων τῆς μεγάλης τῆς ἀληθείας φανερευομένης [?] ὁ Θεὸς Λόγος. Καὶ γὰρ ὡς κάπηγορ[?], καὶ ταὐτὰ λήμμα [?] ἡ ἁγία τῆς Ῥωμαίων Ἐκκλησία τὰς λοιπὰς Ἐκκλησίας καθίσα[?]. Καὶ ἂν αἱ ὀσίφη[?], εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀκλόνητον [?]. Καὶ χρὴ μὴ ἐξετάσεως τὰς κείσεις φέρειν. page.notes: The Greek is only partly legible: each uncertain word is marked [?] and the words are a best reading, not a verified transcription. The Latin is clear except for the hyphenated "su-percilium", which is set with a long s and a printed hyphen at the line end. The catchword "sen-" is the start of the next page's first word, and the paragraph continues there (cont on the next page). No running head, signature or marginal notes are printed on this page.
